title: The Basic example credentials published in RFC 7617
summary: The standard's own example Authorization header, whose decoded user-id and password are the RFC's published sample values.
rationale: The standard publishes the value as an example, which suggests a placeholder, but the standard does not say that the value is never a real credential. Treating documented example literals as placeholders is a policy choice, as it is for provider documentation examples, and no maintainer decision is recorded for this one.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. The value is the standard's published example (a published test value), but whether documented example literals of a protocol are expected silent is a maintainer decision; if the project decides it as policy, the same decision as for provider example keys would apply. Needs a recorded decision with a non-author reviewer.

sources.supports: If the user agent wishes to send the user-id "Aladdin" and password "open sesame", it would use the following header field: Authorization: Basic QWxhZGRpbjpvcGVuIHNlc2FtZQ==

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
